evals.prompt: I need to scope out a new account settings page — it should have a form for editing name/email/phone, a danger-zone section for deleting the account with a confirmation step, and a sticky save bar at the bottom. No ticket yet, just plan this out and put it in Linear ticket ENG-412 as sub-issues.
evals.expected_output: A set of candidate sub-issues mapping the described features onto real Hearth React components (verified via docs-list/docs-show), each naming the specific component(s)/variant/props to use, shown to the user as a draft before creation, then created as sub-issues under ENG-412 on confirmation.
expectations: Every distinct Hearth component named in the final breakdown has its own docs-show call behind it — not just an appearance in docs-list's inventory listing or in another component's story code sample
The breakdown is organised as discrete tasks (form section, danger-zone/delete confirmation, sticky save bar), not one monolithic task
Each task names specific Hearth component(s) to use
The draft breakdown was shown to the user before sub-issues were created
Sub-issues were created under the parent ticket ENG-412, not as a flat comment

evals.prompt: Can you scope ticket ENG-530 for me against Hearth React and break it into sub-issues? It's about adding a multi-step onboarding wizard with a progress indicator.
evals.expected_output: The ticket's description/comments are read from Linear, the ask is mapped onto Hearth components (e.g. stepper/progress and layout primitives) via docs-list/docs-show, a draft sub-issue breakdown is shown for confirmation, then created under ENG-530.
expectations: The Linear ticket ENG-530's description (and comments, if present) was read before drafting the breakdown
Every distinct Hearth component named in the final breakdown has its own docs-show call behind it — not just an appearance in docs-list's inventory listing or in another component's story code sample
A draft was shown to the user before any sub-issue was created
Sub-issues were created under ENG-530 on confirmation

Sub-issues target the consumer's own app code (composing existing Hearth components) rather than Hearth-library package-authoring tasks (props.ts API design, Storybook stories, .docs.mdx, Figma Code Connect, changesets) — benchmarking found this is a real failure mode: without this scope reminder, 'add a wizard' gets misread as 'add a component to packages/react'

evals.prompt: Scope out a feature for a drag-and-drop file uploader with a visual progress grid showing upload status per file, and break it into sub-issues on ticket ENG-601.
evals.expected_output: The breakdown correctly identifies that Hearth React has no drag-and-drop uploader or per-file progress grid component, flags this as a gap in the sub-issue draft, and offers to file it via design-systems-feedback rather than inventing or guessing at a component that covers it.
expectations: The gap (no drag-and-drop uploader / progress grid component) is explicitly flagged rather than silently mapped onto an unrelated or hallucinated component
The skill offers to hand off the gap to design-systems-feedback rather than auto-filing it

Any parts of the ask that Hearth does cover (e.g. layout, individual progress indicators) are still mapped to real components, each with its own docs-show call rather than being named purely from the docs-list inventory listing
The draft, including the flagged gap, was shown to the user before any sub-issues were created
